options.counterfactual: There is a fixed graph H with chromatic number three and ex(n,H)=t_2(n)+O(1) for which no graph simultaneously maximizes edges and cycles at infinitely many orders. Thus 0 belongs to S_2.
options.approach: Search for a forbidden graph whose edge-extremal constructions distribute a bounded number of internal edges between the two bipartition classes, while a construction with fewer edges concentrates them in the larger class. Compare the first-order cycle contributions at odd orders.

options.approach: Examine exceptional vertices and missing cross edges in Simonovits’s structural class. Determine whether a finite modification can gain an edge while decreasing the asymptotic cycle count.

options.approach: Investigate graphs obtained by adding one vertex to a bipartite graph, arranging that deleting an independent set can leave either a star or a matching. Classify the allowable finite internal configurations and test for a discrepancy between edge and cycle optimization.

options.counterfactual: The smallest admissible coefficient is 1/r for every r, and that coefficient belongs to S_r. Constructions involving bounded tree components never produce counterexamples below this value.
options.approach: Generalize the supplied nine-vertex example to chromatic number r+1 by joining it with sufficiently large complete multipartite graphs. Establish the resulting edge-extremal classification and compare its cycles with a matching-based competitor.

options.counterfactual: The smallest admissible coefficient is 1/r for every r, and that coefficient belongs to S_r. Constructions involving bounded tree components never produce counterexamples below this value.
options.approach: Seek a comparison theorem valid under ex(n,H)<t_r(n)+n/r-O(1), checking its hypotheses carefully. Determine whether it rules out counterexamples with bounded-degree internal components.

options.counterfactual: The smallest admissible coefficient is 1/r for every r, and that coefficient belongs to S_r. Constructions involving bounded tree components never produce counterexamples below this value.
options.approach: Recheck the proposed smaller-coefficient construction based on internal three-vertex paths. Look for overlooked edge-extremal configurations or a failure of the claimed extremal classification that restores a simultaneous maximizer.

options.counterfactual: For some r at least three, bounded tree-component constructions already give counterexamples with coefficient strictly below 1/r. The threshold depends on tree shapes and integer part-size adjustments, not merely on the number of added edges.
options.approach: Derive a uniform second-order cycle-count expansion for complete r-partite graphs with bounded tree components added inside one part. Express the comparison in terms of edge count, part-size imbalance, and the number of adjacent internal edge pairs.

options.counterfactual: For some r at least three, bounded tree-component constructions already give counterexamples with coefficient strictly below 1/r. The threshold depends on tree shapes and integer part-size adjustments, not merely on the number of added edges.
options.approach: Construct a single forbidden graph permitting two competing bulk configurations, such as repeated stars and repeated paths of the same order. Arrange a finite edge advantage for the star configuration and test whether the path configuration nevertheless has more cycles.

options.counterfactual: For some r at least three, bounded tree-component constructions already give counterexamples with coefficient strictly below 1/r. The threshold depends on tree shapes and integer part-size adjustments, not merely on the number of added edges.
options.approach: Classify the possible bulk components when the extremal surplus has coefficient below 1/r. Use the classification to bound the cycle advantage of any non-edge-extremal construction and identify the first component size at which that bound permits a counterexample.
